summary.headline: JK Cement Q4 FY26 net sales rose 11% YoY to INR3,614 crore and EBITDA margin hit 18.5%, with FY26 PAT up 21% to INR1,033 crore.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 net sales were INR3,614 crore, up 11% YoY and 15% QoQ, with EBITDA of INR670 crore (18.5% margin) down 9% YoY but up 25% QoQ. Q4 PAT was INR345 crore, down 17% YoY but up 91% QoQ, and FY26 PAT rose 21% to INR1,033 crore. Buxar greenfield commissioned, completing the 6 million tonne Central India expansion, and Muddapur was debottlenecked to 4.5 million tonnes. Management flagged input cost inflation of about INR150 per tonne in Q1 versus Q4, with price hikes of about INR10 per bag so far, and said employee costs will keep rising.

segments.name: Grey cement
segments.commentary: Buxar greenfield (Bihar) commissioned in Q4, completing the 6 MT Central India expansion. Muddapur capacity raised 1 MT to 4.5 MT. Management said capacity totals about 32 MT: North about 15.5 MT, South about 16.5 MT, Central about 12 MT (per the call).

segments.name: White cement and wall putty
segments.commentary: Domestic white cement demand is fully met from domestic plants (Gotan), with no market loss after UAE supply disruption. Prices of white cement and wall putty were raised to pass on chemical cost inflation. Consolidated white cement volume is guided to grow 8-10%.

segments.name: Paints
segments.commentary: FY26 paints top line was about INR380 crore with a loss of about INR40 crore. FY27 guidance is INR500-550 crore revenue, with full-year EBITDA expected to turn marginally positive.

guidance_outlook: FY27 grey cement volume growth is expected to be double-digit, with an incremental 2.5 million tonnes or more, against industry growth of 6-8%.
FY27 capex guided at INR3,500-4,000 crore, of which about INR800-1,000 crore is normal and other capex; FY28 capex guided at INR1,500-2,000 crore.
Jaisalmer integrated plant (4 MT clinker, 7 MT total capacity, cost about INR3,630 crore, INR742 crore spent to March) and Bikaner and Punjab grinding units are expected to commission in H1 FY28.
Nathdwara wall putty plant (6 lakh tonnes) expected to commission by September 2026.
Cost savings of about INR50 per tonne targeted in FY27, driven by green power and AFR in the South and North plants.
Incentive income for FY27 expected around INR250 crore; FY26 was about INR230 crore (INR250-260 crore per the call).
Employee cost for FY27 expected to rise 12-14% YoY on the INR937 crore FY26 base, with about INR250 crore as the quarterly base, after a 10% annual increment from 1 April.
Green power share expected to rise to about 55% by FY27 from 51-52%, with about 80 MW in process; target is 75%.
Panna project expected to finish about INR200-250 crore below the INR2,850 crore budget.
Mining lease for Telangana limestone block (about 500 million tonnes reserves) noted; this may be the next expansion phase after the 2030 plan. Capacity target remains 50 MT by 2030 per management.
capex_capacity: Buxar greenfield commissioned in Q4 FY26, completing the 6 MT Central India expansion; Muddapur raised to 4.5 MT from 3.5 MT.
Jaisalmer integrated unit (4 MT clinker, 7 MT plant) under construction; INR742 crore spent to March against INR3,630 crore cost; commissioning H1 FY28.
Bikaner (2 MT grinding) construction started with main plant equipment ordered; Punjab (2 MT grinding) land acquired and equipment ordered; both expected H1 FY28.
Management said about 4-5% utilisation drop expected after new capacity commissions, but still above national average.
Expanded Central India utilisation estimated at about 65-75%, with run rate at the low end of that range.
demand_pricing: Management expects industry demand growth of 6-8% in FY27 and sees the cement market growing at 6-8% as a fair base despite geopolitical risks to housing.

Average price increase of about INR10 per bag achieved in April and May, against a cost increase of about INR150 per tonne; diesel price increases may add about INR50-60 per tonne if diesel reaches INR11-12.
Competitive intensity in Central India is expected to rise once Jaypee's 5 MT capacity ramps up, with material volume from about Q3 FY27; management said this was expected for 3-4 years.
Rajasthan capacity additions expected in FY28; management plans to use Jaisalmer and the two grinding units to gain share, with the market share expected to gain from shorter distances.
Packing cost pressure has eased after alternative sourcing; packing cost rose by about INR30 crore on volume and price.
Fuel mix in Q4: about 50% petcoke, 12% alternative fuels and the balance Indian coal (heat value basis). Kcal cost INR1.48, rail share 8%, clinker-to-cement ratio 67%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee expenses rise 25% YoY and is INR260 crore a sustainable run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Salaries that were capitalised are now expensed after the Central India plant commissioned, plus added manpower, increments, Labour Code impact and a one-time leave travel assistance provision. Management expects about INR250 crore per quarter base, with a 12-14% full-year rise on INR937 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why was incentive income lower than the guided about INR75 crore per quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Aligarh has availed incentives for its full 10 years, and Rajasthan incentives are not available because GST input credit is taken on the project. Bihar incentives will be accrued only on receipt of the sanction letter. Management guided to about INR250 crore for FY27.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the cost increase has been passed on, and what about the Jaypee plant?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR10 per bag has been passed through in April and May, against about INR150 per tonne of cost increase. Management does not expect a large Jaypee volume impact before Q3 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 volume outlook and cost-saving plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects an incremental 2.5 million tonnes or more in FY27, with cost savings of about INR50 per tonne from green power and AFR.

qa_highlights.question: What are FY27 and FY28 capex plans?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex is INR3,500-4,000 crore, of which about INR800-1,000 crore is normal capex; FY28 is INR1,500-2,000 crore, which excludes uncommitted future expansion.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 50 MT by 2030 target at risk from geopolitical cash-flow pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 2030 plan is unchanged, but a cash-flow shock could delay the next expansion by about 6 months. The next expansion is planned, and capex will be guided only once the Board approves it.

risks_watch: Input cost inflation: about INR150 per tonne Q1 versus Q4, with a further rise to INR200 possible; pricing pass-through so far is only about INR10 per bag.
Diesel price increases could add about INR50-60 per tonne if diesel reaches INR11-12; freight costs rose as well.
Incentive accrual timing (Bihar sanction letter) and loss of Rajasthan and Aligarh incentives.
Central India and Rajasthan competition from Jaypee and new capacity; utilisation may fall 4-5% after new capacity commissions.
Possible regulatory or election-related delays in Punjab; management said none identified so far.
Employee cost run rate and Labour Code impact; FY27 employee cost to rise 12-14%.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volume growth, execution and the 2030 plan, but cautious on near-term cost and geopolitical risk; management gave no firm pricing or diesel-impact figures and deferred several questions ("wait and watch").
